question: Finished work on the engine is sitting on this machine and nowhere else. Three sets of written notes from earlier today have never been sent to the shared copy, and the level edits I am about to fold in will add more. I have been holding rather than sending, because sending is the point where other people and the other tools can see and build on it, and I would rather you set that policy than assume it.

options.name: Let me send finished work up whenever it is done
options.what: Once a piece of work builds clean and the tests pass, it goes to the shared copy without asking you. You stop being interrupted for it.
options.costs: Nothing of your time. Work reaches the shared copy before you have looked at it, so if you dislike something you are reverting it there instead of catching it here.

options.name: Ask you each time
options.what: Nothing leaves this machine until you say so for that specific batch.
options.costs: One short message from you a few times a day, and the work waits in between.

options.name: Keep everything local for now
options.what: Nothing is sent at all until you revisit this.
options.costs: Free today. Every finished piece exists in exactly one place, so a lost machine is a lost week, and the other tools keep reading an older version of this engine than the one I am working on.

recommend.because: Everything I would send has already been through the full build and the whole test suite before it goes, so the review you would be doing at that moment is one the machine has already done. The live risk is the other direction: your own level edits have been sitting unsaved for four days and three sets of notes for one day, all in a single copy.

detail: Three docs-only commits sit unpushed on aeon master: 3e30ccdd, d67730ed, d77137fc (2026-08-23 04:15 to 04:19 EDT). origin/master is at 139995f2. The STRAND parcel will add two data commits plus a sigil-side repin and refreeze that must be pushed as a pair with them. Empyrean attempted to consolidate this suite-wide and then agreed a hub relay cannot carry an authorization.

question: Your level edits from the nineteenth and twentieth of this month, the painting you did in the editor and the collision shapes under it, were never saved into the project history. They are loose in the working copy and have been for four days. Folding them in also means rebuilding the game and re-checking the frozen size records our assembler keeps, because level data is baked into the cartridge image. That is what I would start on, and I want to know if you would rather I started somewhere else.

options.name: Fold in my level edits first
options.what: Your painting and collision work becomes part of the project history and is safe. The game gets rebuilt and re-verified around it.
options.costs: A couple of hours, most of it me waiting on builds and the test suite. Nothing else on my list is waiting behind it.

options.name: Do the small toolchain change first
options.what: A short alignment change our assembler asked for goes in ahead of everything else.
options.costs: Under an hour of work, but it needs a fresh toolchain build before it will even read the source, and your level edits stay loose the whole time.

options.name: Push on the effects work instead
options.what: I carry on with the half that still stands between an effect you build in the editor and that effect actually running in the game.
options.costs: A day or more before there is anything to see, and your level edits stay loose the whole time.

recommend.because: It is the only thing on my list where your own work is currently unprotected, it is the shortest of the three, and it clears the ground for the other two rather than competing with them.

question: The background art fills every tile slot it has, so the editor cannot add an animated band to it. Should this lane make a simplified test-only background to free room, or does that belong to the editor lane? There may also be a third answer where nobody needs to make art at all.

options.what: Ask the editor lane first whether a band can be made by reusing tiles the art already has
options.costs: One message and a short wait. If the answer is yes, no art work is needed by anyone and the whole question goes away. If no, you have lost an hour and still choose between the two below.

options.what: This lane makes a simplified test-only background
options.costs: A few hours here, and the picture gets plainer for testing only - your shipped art is untouched and this is inside the permission you already gave. It unblocks the editor lane without them waiting on anyone.
They own the art tools and would likely do a better-looking job, but they are the lane currently blocked, so they would be unblocking themselves and it lands behind their other work.

recommend: Ask the editor lane first whether a band can be made by reusing tiles the art already has
because: Our own notes say promotion - reusing existing tiles, adding none - is a working route, and it is the only option that might cost nobody any art work at all. It is one message against a few hours, and it cannot make the other two choices worse. If it comes back no, I would then recommend this lane doing it, because they are the lane that is stuck.

question: The background art has no room for an animated band. d-4 asked you to pick which lane does the art work - that was the wrong question and I am withdrawing it. Our own notes say YOU generate this art with your constrained generator and judge it by eye, so the art step is not a lane's to take. There may also be a route where no new art is needed at all. Do you want to regenerate now, or wait to hear whether that route works?

options.what: Wait for the answer on whether a band can reuse tiles the art already has
options.costs: A short wait. If it works, nothing needs regenerating and you spend no time at all. The editor lane is being asked now, so the answer should not be long.

options.what: Regenerate the background now with 320 as the generator's limit, without waiting
options.costs: Your time at the generator, plus a look on screen to judge it. It removes the uncertainty immediately and cannot be wasted - the extra room is useful either way. But if the reuse route works, you spent that time for nothing.

options.what: Leave it entirely until you next feel like touching the art
options.costs: Costs nothing now, and nothing here is urgent. The effects work stays finished-but-unproven until an animated band exists somewhere, so the first real end-to-end test keeps waiting.

recommend: Wait for the answer on whether a band can reuse tiles the art already has
because: It is the only option that might cost you nothing, the question is already being asked, and none of the other choices get worse for waiting. Worth saying plainly: the 320 figure is not a target anyone needs you to hit exactly - your own instruction was that it just has to still look slightly reasonable, and the number was picked to be generous and tightened later rather than squeezed.

question: An animated background band is stored in a slot whose size was fixed back when no act had one, and a real band needs about four thousand times that. Fixing the slot is easy; the question is how big to make it. A band's size depends entirely on how big an author draws it, and the legal range runs from 302 bytes to about 112 KB - a 380x spread. Whatever we pick, an author who draws a bigger band than that gets a build failure, so this is really a question about how much background animation you want to be possible without an engine change.

options.name: Pick a generous ceiling now and refuse politely above it
options.what: We reserve room for a band up to 16 tiles wide by 8 tall - about eight times the one Aurora just drew, and comfortably inside the spare room that already exists next to it. Anything bigger stops the build with a message naming the limit, instead of the cryptic collision we get today. Authors never think about this again until they hit the ceiling.
options.costs: About 32 KB of cartridge space set aside whether or not an act uses it. You have roughly 350 KB spare, so it is not tight. If you ever want a band bigger than that, raising it is a small change but it is a change.

options.name: Reserve enough for the biggest band that could ever exist
options.what: Room for a band covering every tile the background has. No author can ever hit a limit, and this question never comes back.
options.costs: About 112 KB set aside permanently, which is very nearly all the spare room in that part of the cartridge. It would leave that neighbourhood with almost nothing left for anything else later.

options.name: Re-measure the layout every time the band changes size
options.what: No space is wasted and no ceiling exists. The layout is recomputed to fit whatever the author actually drew.
options.costs: Every time you resize a band, the cartridge layout has to be re-measured and re-approved in the assembler's repo - a deliberate act in a different project. It turns a normal art tweak into a cross-project chore, which cuts against the whole point of the effects work: that something you build in the editor just reaches the game.

recommend.because: It is the only option that costs you nothing at authoring time and does not spend the room you may want later. It also matches how this engine already handles the same kind of limit elsewhere - the number of bands is a declared ceiling with a guard that names it - so it is the consistent choice rather than a new idea. And the failure it produces is a sentence telling an author their band is too big, which is the failure you want if you are ever going to hit one.

detail: ojz_bg_anim's frozen allotment is 2 bytes (measured from the disabled stub: BgAnim_Table u16 = 0 plus Data.empty). Section size derives exactly as 46 + cols*rows*8*32 (2 + 12 + 32 header/record/pointer bytes + cols*rows*BANKS*32 bank blob); aurora's authored 8x4 band = 8238, matching the observed span [0x3B270,0x3D29E) exactly. Range over legal author geometries: 1x1=302, 8x4=8238, 16x8=32814, 32x14 (all 448 tiles)=114734. Slack before the hardware-pinned dac_banks anchor at 0x48000 is ~119 KB. Mechanism: native.rs:2947-2970 makes a section an anchor (Pinned) when its frozen true base exceeds the running chain end, so growth collides with the next pinned chain rather than flowing. Precedent for the ceiling shape: BGANIM_MAX_BANDS, a declared ceiling with a span guard (tools/test_bg_emit.py::TestBgAnimBandCeiling). Raised independently by the aurora lane (from band arithmetic) and this lane (from sigil's placement mechanism) - different enumeration parameters, so corroboration rather than echo.
